newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lowers forex mini-band to 1.050-1.055 reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lowers forex mini-band to 1.050-1.055 reais.

text.p: Brazil will lower its foreign exchange mini-band to a range between 1.050-1.055 reais against the dollar as of the beginning of trade on Wednesday, Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco said.

Speaking at a news conference shortly after the Central Bank announced a new large foreign exchange band of 1.05-1.14 reais per dollar, Franco said the adjustments signalled foreign exchange rate policy would continue exactly as it has been.
"From tomorrow everything will be absolutely as it has been," Franco told reporters.
"We are continuing with something we started one and a half years ago," Franco said refering to the introduction of the interband foreign exchange rate policy in 1995.

Franco said the Central Bank had moved forward the introduction of the new large band when it realized the market was anxious and speculating about a change in foreign exchange policy as the dollar-real parity approached the former large band ceiling.

"Everyone in the market had been anticipating that the ceiling would be raised. We brought the decision forward by a few weeks because we didn't want to wait until the last possible date as this would have caused anxiety," he said.
He said the new 1.050-1.055 mini-band, which is just 0.1 percent lower than the previous mini-band and was announced earlier on Tuesday, was evidence there had been no change in policy.
"(We did this) exactly to show there are no surprises or novelties in introducing this change," said Franco.
